A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CE-OCR work, and their supplied text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. v3 ends after the references despite appendix cross-references; v4 supplies Appendices A–K. No essential reading gaps were encountered.

before.justification: v3 reports original human-annotation comparisons, OCR benchmark experiments, ensemble and routing evaluations, ablations, and computational measurements in Section 4.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and supplies additional calibration, output-cleaning, computational, and ensemble results in its appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions retain pairwise consensus entropy, inverse-entropy weighting, token aggregation, and threshold-based routing to a stronger VLM. v4 specifies previously underexplained probability construction and algorithm details, but does not establish a replacement procedure or new method component.

E1.justification: OCRBench, OCRBench-V2, CCOCR, the curated 1,000-page dataset, and the beyond-OCR VQA categories are already covered in v3. v4 adds source descriptions, diagnostics, and detailed results within this retained coverage, without establishing an added dataset or task.

E2.justification: VL-Uncertainty, cited only as related work in v3, becomes an evaluated comparator in v4 Table 9. Best Single, ROVER, and CE-Ensemble remain in that comparison; the existing VLM-as-Judge and Self-Consistency baselines are retained.

E3.justification: Added diagnostic protocols use ECE, Brier score, and AUC with related versus diverse reference models (Table 14), compare original versus cleaned GPT-4o outputs (Table 16), and report additional filtering thresholds (Table 18). The main experiments retain their decoding settings, ensemble sizes, and routing threshold.

E4.justification: Appendix B supplies substantial additional diagnostics: bandwidth/correlation sensitivity, calibration and reference-diversity analysis, detailed identical-model sampling results, and GPT-4o verbosity cleaning. Appendix G adds five qualitative cases. Tables 12 and 13 repeat existing comparisons rather than constituting new ablations.

E5.justification: Table 15 newly exposes individual scores from the three stochastic runs, whereas v3 reports aggregate identical-model gains. The three-run, temperature-0.7 setting was already disclosed; there is no documented increase in runs or addition of confidence intervals, seeds, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing main-table scores are retained, but v4 adds VL-Uncertainty results and substantial calibration, cleaning, runtime, and ensemble results. Table 22 includes mixed CCOCR outcomes, such as an ensemble scoring 77.23 versus its best single model's 77.67. Section 4.6 also corrects ROVER's reported Doc-VQA/Math declines from 71.8%/96.8% to 42.1%/92.0%, without changing the underlying table scores.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an explicit normalized-edit-similarity and probability definition with a worked entropy example. Appendix E specifies the adaptive covariance formula. These extend the mathematical specification, but no theorem or proof is added; the existing entropy, weighting, and routing equations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: training-free CE estimates reliability through agreement, and ensemble/routing improves OCR efficiently. The headline 42.1% verification improvement and 8.2% OCR gain with 7.3% routing are unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations of ROVER and VL-Uncertainty failures, GPT-4o verbosity effects, and the limitations of applying classification-calibration metrics to CE. Appendix K explicitly discusses specialized-domain embeddings, multiple-model resource requirements, and application-specific threshold calibration. These materially expand mechanisms and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: The appendix supplies previously unavailable pseudocode, judge/router/OCR prompts, document sources, annotation rules and interface, software versions, model-version information, and kernel-tuning details. v4 also adds code and annotated-data access information. These substantially improve documentation, although numerical values for the kernel/grid hyperparameters remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v4 adds seven cited works covering RAG, dialogue, cross-modal generation, and structured consistency verification, with limited corresponding background expansion. It also develops the comparison with the already-cited VL-Uncertainty. The principal positioning around unsupervised OCR reliability remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds a substantial explanatory structure through Appendices A–K and a contents page, organizing data curation, annotation, algorithms, prompts, evaluations, and limitations. Most main-text prose and section order remain, with localized rewrites clarifying verification versus ensemble/routing, plus revised author information and new acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures 6–14, Tables 12–26, two algorithm displays, and prompt boxes, including plots, an annotation screenshot, qualitative panels, and extensive ensemble tables. Some displays reproduce existing evidence, notably Tables 12/13 and Figure 6; others add content. Main-text figures and tables are also repositioned and several captions revised.

improvement.justification: The appendix supplies supporting material missing from v3, while the new baseline and corrected ROVER percentages strengthen evaluation. However, Section 3.1's new probability normalization conflicts with its zero-entropy claim for identical outputs. Figures 10–11 also reverse the displayed human-quality labels and swap CE/VLM-as-Judge scores in their captions. These contradictions affect the central metric and qualitative validation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment despite improved completeness.
